title: The Missing Chart

evidence.name: Tea Ring on the Velvet
evidence.text: A damp brown ring on the velvet where the chart lay, with a crumb of shortbread beside it. The museum has a strict rule: no food, no drink, no exceptions. Whoever lifted the chart had been in a tea room first.

evidence.name: Visitors' Book
evidence.text: The last signature before closing, in a neat round hand: 'M. Tulloch, Lerwick. Just looking.' Beside it, a tiny doodle of an OXO motif. Plenty of people sign this book. Few of them doodle in knitting.

evidence.name: Dyer's Order Book
evidence.text: Last week's order: four skeins each of moorit, sea blue, madder red and white, 'M. Tulloch, for a cosy'. That is a great deal of cosy. It is also, to the skein, the colours on the missing chart.

evidence.name: Squared Paper
evidence.text: Under the tea-room counter: squared paper with a half-coloured chart in wax crayon. The border is the museum chart's border, cross for cross. This is a copy in progress, and the copyist has got as far as the snowflakes.

evidence.name: The Dyer's Jumper
evidence.text: A jumper on the dyer's needles with three colours in one row. A true Fair Isle never uses more than two in a row, so this is not the chart's work, merely the dyer's enthusiasm. Lovely, wrong and entirely her own.

evidence.name: Fiddler's Manuscript
evidence.text: Squared lines of black dots on ruled paper: at a glance, a chart. In fact a reel called 'The Knitter's Revenge'. The fiddler writes his tunes on whatever is to hand, which this week is the back of a ferry timetable.

evidence.name: Shavings by the Case
evidence.text: A scatter of pale shavings by the display case. The boat builder works in the hall next door and sheds wood the way a spaniel sheds hair. Suspicious only if you have never met a boat builder.

suspects.name: The Boat Builder
suspects.wrong: A knitting chart? I build boats, not jumpers! The only thing I have ever stolen is a march on the weather. Away and look again.

suspects.name: The Dyer
suspects.wrong: Me? I'd never take a chart. I can read one on sight, which is a good deal safer than nicking it. And three colours in a row is a style, thank you.

suspects.name: The Session Fiddler
suspects.wrong: Pinch a pattern? I can't even pinch a tune without apologising. That is a reel, not a chart. Mostly.

suspects.name: Marjory Tulloch
suspects.right: Oh, you've found me out. Ingrid said the chart was too fragile to lend, and it's fading, and I only wanted to knit the museum a copy for the shop window. It's in my knitting bag. I was going to put it back on Friday. I was going to put it back so nicely.

steps.text: Speak to Registrar Elsie Nicolson in the Shetland Museum.
Look at the empty display case in the Shetland Museum.
Check the visitors' book on the table in the Shetland Museum.
Ask the Boat Builder in the Shetland Museum.
Ask the Dyer at Fair Isle Knitwear.
Ask the Session Fiddler at The Lounge.
Search the tables at the Harbour Tea Room.
Have a word with the Tea Room Lady at the Harbour Tea Room.
Report back to Registrar Elsie Nicolson in the Shetland Museum.

accuse_hint: Registrar Elsie Nicolson is waiting at the Shetland Museum.
closed: The chart is back in its case, a faded copy hangs in the shop window, and Marjory has been appointed Honorary Keeper of the Squared Paper. The tea room is now, officially, a museum annexe.
